title: Rethinking Individual Risk and Aggregation in Survival Analysis: A Latent Mechanism Framework
summary: Survival analysis provides a well-established framework for modeling time-to-event data, with hazard and survival functions formally defined as population-level quantities. In applied work, however, these quantities are often interpreted as representing individual-level risk, despite the absence of a clear generative account linking individual risk mechanisms to observed survival data.
